title: refactor(sim): law (d)'s prior readers read the stock through Columns
body:
## What changed

M7.3 step 2/6 (#26 umbrella, split in https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/26#issuecomment-6754685656).

Law (d)'s prior-stock readers, `verify::prior_surface` and `verify::acquit_by_prior`, took `&Dexel`, which names the column engine directly. They now take `&Columns<'_>`, the M7.3 column seam that a column or field `Stock` already answers through.

- **`Columns` gains `Columns::of_grid(&Dexel)`:** a borrowed bare rest grid, read through the same seam. The reader's source becomes an internal `Source::{Grid, Field}`, so a reader no longer needs a whole `Stock`.
- **`Columns` gains `cell()`, `center(ix, iy)` and `origin()`.**
- **The operation layer** (`drill_prior::PriorRead::surface`, `generate.rs`'s acquittal) still holds the program-ahead grid as a `Dexel`, so it wraps it with `of_grid`. #586 moves that holder onto `Stock`, and the call then becomes `stock.columns()?`.
- **Scope corrected from the research:** `solid_rest` names no `Dexel`. `carry::Body` uses `Dexel` as storage, not as a reader, so that move goes with #586/#589. It's recorded on #585 and in `docs/decisions/585-prior-readers-on-columns.md`.

The change is behaviour-neutral: `Columns` maps a point to its column by the column engine's own formula, so a grid read through it answers identically.

## How tested

- **The existing `verify::prior` unit tests pass unchanged, 4/4**, wrapped in `Columns::of_grid`.
- **New `crates/sim/tests/prior_columns.rs`, 2/2:**
  - `the_prior_surface_reads_alike_through_a_grid_and_a_field`: inside the hole, across its rim and on the raw top, the column and field stocks agree within 1e-6. It reads the hole floor at 15 and the raw top at 25.
  - `a_dive_is_acquitted_alike_on_either_engine_and_through_a_bare_grid`: a column stock, a field stock and a bare grid acquit the same dive and keep the same conviction.
- **`scripts/gate.sh quick`** escalated to batch. geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion and app all pass, and clippy `-D warnings` is clean on every crate. The only reds are the 3 headless-GPU ui tests, which are environmental on this host.
- **Named:** drill_prior 12, drill_reach 6, carried_verify 8, setup_carry 9, stock_columns 3.
- No golden or snapshot changed. Branched from v0.16.0, which the fork's main is synced to.

## Not exercised

Nothing user-visible changes, so there is no GUI or machine check.

title: fix(post): an explicit M5 after a probe's tool change in every post
body:
**Stacked on #579** (#570, probe search limit and feed-only approach). It includes #579's commits until that PR merges.

## What changed
Every mill post now writes an explicit spindle stop between a probe's tool change and length offset and its first move. Today the probe is safe on a Tormach only because PathPilot's `M6` stops the spindle, which is a property of the control, not something the program says.
- **Rule:** in `startPreamble`, `probeStop = spindleWait && !(sRpm > 0)`. Only a probe states 0 rpm, because tools refuse 0. After the spindle block and before coolant, the post writes the stop.
- **Per post:**
  - Fanuc, Haas, Tormach, Sinumerik, Heidenhain: `M5`.
  - Mazak: `MOTOFF`, its own stop word.
  - Fanuc Lathe: untouched (no probing).
- **Unchanged:** cutting sections and older streams post byte-identical output.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/574-probe-m5.md`.

**Stack merge (`fd1076af`):** #579 branched from a main older than #174's protected probe moves, so merging it hit conflicts in three Fanuc goldens and broke `probe_guard`. The merge commit resolves both.
- #579's new feed from the safe plane down to the approach plane now posts as a protected move: `G31` plus the `#5063` alarm on Fanuc, `G38.3` plus the `#5070` check on Tormach.
- `probe_guard` expects one more protected move per mode.
- `fanuc/probe_corner.nc` and `tormach/probe_guard_moves.nc` are regenerated to match.

#579 will need the same resolution when it takes main.

**Golden diffs from #574 itself:** each file gains one `M5` line right after the `G43` line:
- `fanuc/probe_bore_centre.nc`
- `fanuc/probe_corner.nc`
- `fanuc/probe_corner_negative.nc`
- `fanuc/probe_edge_negative_x.nc`
- `tormach/probe_guard_moves.nc`

Until #526 merges, some posts still write a probe's spindle start (`S0 M3`) before the new stop. The flag is computed separately, so it works in either merge order; Heidenhain will have a small hand-merge next to #526's lines.

## How tested
- **New `probe_spindle_stop`, all six mill posts:**
  - `a_probe_section_stops_its_spindle_after_the_tool_change_on_every_mill_post`: the stop comes after the tool change and offset, before the first move, and nothing restarts the spindle. It failed before the change.
  - `a_cutting_section_states_no_spindle_stop_before_its_first_move`: the control case.
- **Also passing:** probe_op, probe_guard, inverted_probe, conformance, posting, tormach_post, fanuc_post, heidenhain_block_form, sinumerik_safe_retract, plus #579's probe_search, probe_pick and probe_reach, and all camcraft-post tests. Clippy (post and app) is clean.

## Not exercised (draft)
A Hub or machine run of a probe program with the new `M5`. It is a defensive stop on an already-stopped spindle.

Changelog: Every mill post writes an explicit spindle stop (M5; MOTOFF on Mazak) after a probe's tool change and length offset, before its first move (#574)

title: fix(app): a probe searches a short way past the face and feeds below the safe plane
body:
## What changed

Found on the contributor's real Tormach 770MX during #521's hands-on probe test. Two things alarmed the operator: a new Probe op searched **5 mm** past the expected face (`G38.2 Z-0.1969`), and its approach was a **rapid straight down** to 0.197 in over the part.

- **Shorter default search:** a new Probe op's probe distance is `default_overtravel(tolerance) = max(2 × tolerance, 1 mm)`, which is 1 mm for the seeded 0.5 mm tolerance. Existing documents keep their stated value.
- **Named, non-blocking advisory:** a new `Warning::ProbeSearch` flags any probe distance past `SEARCH_LIMIT_MM` (2 mm). Like `Scallop`, it never holds the post, so old 5 mm documents still post. It is wired into the UI warning list, MCP `job` and `warned_moves`.
- **Protected approach:** `probing::probe_cycle` now opens with a positioning rapid that ends at the **safe plane** over the first start, then **feeds** at the seek feed down to the approach point. No probe rapid runs below the safe plane. The positioning rapid is zero-length in the path's frame, because the path cannot know the tool-change position, and every post writes it as its positioning block. That keeps the Fanuc post from feeding diagonally from the tool change.
- **Probe page hint:** it now says the distance is a search **limit**, not a destination, and that over 2 mm is flagged.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/570-probe-search-and-approach.md`.

## Readings

- **Before**, Fanuc golden: `G00 X-22 Y5 Z25` (a rapid to the approach point).
- **After**, the same golden:
  ```
  G00 X-22 Y5 Z50
  G01 X-22 Y5 Z25 F300
  ```
- The 770MX run with a hand-edited approach-as-feed and a Z-0.05 search touched at Z≈0. G54 Z moved from -8.3252 to -8.3259, a 0.0007 in correction, in line with a manual 0.0009 check.

## How tested

- **New `crates/app/tests/probe_search.rs`, 3/3:**
  - `a_new_probe_op_searches_a_short_way_past_the_face`: the seed follows its tolerance and draws no advisory.
  - `a_deep_search_is_named_and_never_holds_the_post`
  - `below_the_safe_plane_a_probe_only_feeds`: Face, Edge, Corner, Bore and Boss. It **fails on the old cycle** with "positioning ends at the safe plane, not 15".
- **Fixtures:** `probe_pick` and `probe_reach` move to the new 1 mm default, since they stand for new ops. `probe_op` and `fanuc_post` keep 5 mm, standing for old documents.
- **Goldens:** the 3 Fanuc probe goldens are regenerated, with one line added each. No snapshot changed.
- **`scripts/gate.sh quick`:** sim, motion and app suites ran 2307 passed, 0 failed. The ui suites are green except the 3 known headless-GPU tests on this host ("No suitable graphics adapter found"), which are environmental.
- **Named:** probe_search 3, probe_op 11, probe_reach 5, probe_pick 9, fanuc_post 11, posting 17, conformance 6.
- **Clippy** on app, ui, motion and sim with `-D warnings`: clean.
- Fork synced at v0.15.0.

## Not exercised

The post straight from this build on the real 770MX. The hand-edited equivalent ran clean, but PathPilot flagged "Axis XY not specified" on the hand edit, which this post's `startXY` G0 X Y avoids.

**Stacked after this, by the M3:** #574 (an explicit M5 after a probe's tool change), then #575 (report the deviation).

Changelog: A new probe op searches only 1 mm past the expected face (was 5 mm), a probe distance over 2 mm is flagged, and a probe never rapids below the safe plane - it feeds down to its approach point (#570)

Fixes #570

title: fix(app): turning a part keeps a square stock square
body:
**Stacked on #566** (#561, locate the part in a fixture). It includes #566's commits until that PR merges.

## What changed
Turning a part on the Model page rotated its stock rigidly with it (`move_model.rs`), so a square blank came out tilted. #566 fixed this for locate only. Now every `MoveModel` that **turns** the part uses the same square-stock rule (`stock_follow::keep_square`):
- **Square stocks:** a box or cylinder whose axes lie along the setup's axes (any quarter turn) keeps its orientation. It is refitted around the part's new place, keeping each side's allowance, measured in the stock's own frame before the move.
- **Quarter turns refit too; the block doesn't rotate with the part.** One rule for one gesture, so 89.99° and 90° give the same kind of blank. Top stays top, so a "+top for facing" allowance never moves onto a side. A yaw quarter turn refits to the same size anyway.
- **Unchanged cases:**
  - Translation-only moves keep the old rigid carry, with no refit and no mesh rebuild.
  - A copied-from-model stock, or one already off the axes, still turns rigidly with the part.
- **Locate:** `MoveModel::locating` now just calls `MoveModel::new`.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/571-movemodel-square-stock.md`.

## How tested
- **Updated pin:** `commands_undo::moving_one_part_carries_existing_stock_and_undo_restores_both` keeps its intent (the stock follows, undo restores both). After a 90° yaw plus a move, the stock stays square and wraps the part.
- **New `move_model_stock`:**
  - a 30° turn keeps a box stock square with each allowance, and undo/redo are exact;
  - a 30° turn keeps a cylinder upright;
  - translation-only moves carry the stock rigidly as before;
  - a turned or copied stock still turns rigidly.
  - The pin and both 30° tests failed before the change.
- **Gate:** app lib (105), commands_undo, fixture_locate(_stock), setup_align, plane_align(_edges), top_stock, setup_stock_source, stock_stamp, project_roundtrip, wcs_align, pick_doors, stock_view, stock_play, the ui models tests and the ui locate tests pass. Clippy is clean.

## Not exercised
A hands-on GUI turn on the Model page.

Changelog: Turning a part on the Model page keeps a square box or cylinder stock square to the machine, refitted around the part with its per-side allowances; moves that only slide the part carry the stock as before (#571)

Fixes #571

title: feat(app,ui): part axes in the work plane by edge or two points; plane alignment picks faces only
body:
Two linked setup-page alignment changes on one branch. Both edit the same alignment picks, so they would conflict as separate PRs. The fork is synced at v0.15.0; branched with upstream/main merged.

## #557: set the part's X and Y in the work plane by an edge or two points (`bc2f5353`)
- **App** (`pick/axis.rs`, `turn_in_plane`):
  - **Pick:** an `AxisPick`, one straight edge or two vertices plus a flip, is read through the setup's current part alignment, so it composes after a face-to-plane lay.
  - **Turn:** the pick is projected onto the setup's XY, and the part turns about setup Z around its centre, so it stays on its spot of the table.
  - **Both axes:** the primary one (Y by default, or X) is laid exactly. The other is only checked: a parallel or left-handed pair is refused, never averaged.
  - **One axis:** the other follows right-handed (X = Y × Z).
  - **Precision:** quarter turns snap exactly.
- **Command:** the existing undoable `AlignPartToSetup` (new `turn_in_plane` / `check_turn` entries). The stock follows, linked setups follow, ops go stale and undo clears that. The same `part_alignment` field is used, so there is **no project-file change**.
- **Refused by name:** a face, a closed or curved edge, a single point, coincident points, an edge mixed with a point, a pick that isn't the part, a stale pick, a direction within 5° of the plane normal, a parallel or left-handed X/Y, nothing picked, a non-finite result, and "already holds the part that way".
- **UI:** a new "Axes in the plane - pick an edge or two points for +Y and/or +X" section on the setup page and the Setups overview.
  - Per axis: by Edge or by Two points, a Pick toggle, and Flip.
  - Then Primary, **Apply axes** (greyed with the reason; it shows the turn in degrees first) and Clear.
- **MCP:** `set_part_axes`.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/557-axis-by-edge.md`.

## #554: the setup page's plane alignment picks faces only (`7d641c8b`)
- **Plane row:** it now reads "Lay on a plane - pick a face" and arms Face mode, so a click beside an edge takes the face.
- **Removed:** the #330 two-edge plane mode. `pick::lay_on_plane` refuses an edge by name ("an edge cannot set a plane; pick a flat face (edges set an axis: Axes in the plane)").
- **Unchanged:** 3-2-1 alignment and operation-geometry edge picks.
- **Decision record:** `docs/decisions/554-plane-pick-faces-only.md`.

## How tested
- **App `axis_align` (10):**
  - an edge at 30° → +Y, about the centre;
  - two points as X;
  - flip;
  - both axes, Y or X primary, plus the left-handed and parallel refusals;
  - a tilted pick projects cleanly;
  - near-normal and degenerate picks, a curved arc and a closed rim are refused;
  - undo and redo;
  - composes after a face lay;
  - stale, and undo clears it.
- **MCP:** `set_part_axes_turns_the_part_from_an_edge_or_two_points`.
- **UI:**
  - `setup_axis_tests` (3): edge → Apply → undo and redo, with a face refused; two points plus flip; an upright edge greys Apply with the reason.
  - New `plane_face_pick`: a real viewport click 4 px inside a face takes the face with the plane row armed, and the edge with an axis row armed.

title: feat(app,ui): locate the part in a fixture (or the fixture on the part) by face/point mates
body:
Locates the part in an imported fixture, or the fixture on the part, by face and point mates (#561, part of #339). Branched from the fork's main (synced at v0.15.0) with upstream/main merged.

## What changed
**Solver:** `fixture_locate.rs`, with the pure solve in `fixture_locate_solve.rs`. It takes one to three mates in the fixture's setup frame: face–face, point–point, point-on-face and face-on-point. It returns one rigid transform and never touches the WCS.
- **Order:** 3-2-1 fixturing. The first face mate opposes the normals by the shortest turn. The second turns the part about that normal. A third must already agree. Then each mate fixes the remaining free motion, in mate order.
- **Nudge:** after the mates, a turn about the first fixture normal, then an X/Y/Z shift.
- **Pick reader:** `pick/mate.rs` reuses `outward_normal` and `facets_centroid` (#187/#330).

**Commands** (`commands/locate.rs`):
- `LocatePart` moves the part through `MoveModel`, so the stock follows. In a turned setup (#326) it composes into `AlignPartToSetup` instead.
- `LocateFixture` moves the fixture by the inverse, through `MoveFixture`.
- `Locate` wraps both for the UI and MCP. Every locate is one undo step.

**Refused by name at creation:**
- **Bodies:** no fixture, the machine table, a model that isn't a fixture, no part, or a pick on the wrong body.
- **Picks:** an edge or curved face, a zero-area face, or two mates on the same point or face.
- **Solve:** faces that can't oppose, contradicting mates, zero mates or more than three, a non-finite nudge, or "nothing would move".

**Interpenetration warns rather than refuses.** A sampled inside test (the fixture mesh's ray law) names the part, the fixture and a point.

**UI:**
- **Fixtures page:** a **Locate part…** verb on each row.
- **Model page:** a locate row.
- **Form:** Move the part / Move the fixture, Offset X/Y/Z, Turn, **Apply locate** (greyed with the solve's reason) and Remove last.
- **Picks:** part first, then fixture, routed through the existing face and vertex picking.

**MCP:** a `locate_part` tool. `list_features` accepts a fixture.

## Choices that differ from the issue (decision file: `docs/decisions/561-locate-part-fixture.md`)
- **A moved fixture doesn't mark the setup's ops stale.** That keeps the existing rule that workholding never stales a toolpath. The collision check re-judges live instead, and a test pins it. Moving the part does mark them stale, and undo clears it.
- **Maintainer's call: in an unaligned setup the part moves through `MoveModel`.** That changes its document placement, so in a multi-setup document it also moves the part in the other setups, and their ops go stale and need regenerating. A translation-only setup alignment was avoided, because it would make the setup count as aligned and refuse every non-2D op. An alternative is to refuse a locate in an unaligned multi-setup document and point to aligning the setup first.
- **Deferred:** point-pair mates don't turn the part (only face mates orient it); there's no preview before Apply; per-setup part placement for unaligned multi-setup documents.

## How tested
- **App `fixture_locate` (11):**
  - a face mate makes the faces coplanar with opposed normals;
  - floor, jaw and stop give a full location;
  - the offset and turn are exact;
  - LocateFixture moves the fixture, not the part;
  - undo and redo;
  - point mates;
  - degenerate and conflicting picks are refused by name;
  - the interpenetration warning;
  - ops go stale and undo clears it;
  - a moved fixture is re-judged live while the path stays fresh;
  - the turned-setup case.
- **MCP:** `mcp_setup::locate_part_seats_the_part_on_the_fixture_by_feature_ids`.
- **UI:**
  - `locate_tests`: apply a locate from the Fixtures page, with undo and redo; the Model page moves the fixture to the part;
  - `fixture_rows`: the locate tools fit inside the pane on both pages;
  - `structural.rs`: no locate draft is armed by default.
- **Regressions:** `fixtures`, `fixture_ux`, `fixture_mesh`, `fixture_mesh_posed`, `setup_align`, `plane_align`, `commands_undo`, `project_roundtrip`, `mcp`, `mcp_setup` and `mcp_pick` all pass. ui lib passes 379 of 380; the failure is the headless-GPU test, which needs a graphics adapter this machine doesn't have. Clippy (app and ui, `-D warnings`) is clean.

A GUI hands-on check (the picks in the viewport). That will be driven headless next.

body:
**Replaces #376** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

**Stacked on #333** (`issue/257-gcode-comments`, which also edits `tormach.cps`). This diff includes #333's commits until it merges; the #362 work is the last commit (55b7b83).

## What changed
`assets/posts/tormach.cps` gains `onProbeMove` / `onProbeRetreat` / `onProbeResult` in LinuxCNC/PathPilot words, so a Probe op posts on the Tormach mills instead of being refused by name.

**The touch move**
- It is `G38.2`. The control halts with an error when contact never comes, or when the probe is already tripped at the start, so the post writes no no-contact test of its own.
- XY is positioned first, so a probe never starts from an unknown XY.
- `G38.3` plus a `#5070` test was rejected: it hands that safety from the control to our own branch.

**Reading the trip**
- It is read from `#5061`–`#5063`. These are in the coordinate system the G38 ran in, in program units, so they compare directly with the expected values.

**Back-off and tolerance alarm**
- The back-off is incremental (`G91 G1 … G90`).
- A deviation past the tolerance runs `o9nn if [ABS[#19x] GT tol]` / `(MSG, …)` / `M2` / `o9nn endif`, with a unique O-word per test.
- `M2`, not `M0`, so the operator can't resume onto a wrong offset. `(ABORT,…)` is not in the stable LinuxCNC reference.

**Setting the offset**
- `G10 L20 P<n> X[#5420-#190] …`: the current position in the active offset, minus the deviation. It is exact in either unit.
- `G10 L2` from `#5221+20×slot` was rejected: the reference doesn't say which unit the stored offsets use, so a G21 program on an inch-configured control could mix units.
- With no offset to set, it writes `(MSG, CHECK PROBE RESULT …)` then `M0`.

**Preamble**
- A section at 0 rpm (a touch probe) writes no spindle start, no belt note and no coolant.

**Arming**
- Nothing is written. PathPilot's probe input is always live, and the probe type is a Settings-tab choice.

The sources for every word are in `docs/decisions/362-tormach-probe.md`: the LinuxCNC G-code reference, overview and o-code pages, and Tormach's PathPilot post-processor guidelines and G38.x pages. No other CAM system's output was read.

title: feat(app): recognise pockets and slots and turn them into operations
body:
## What changed

Pocket and slot recognition, headless (app layer and MCP; no GUI changes).

- **`camcraft_app::recognize`** (new module: `mod`, `walls`, `shape`, `op`):
  - `pockets_of(world, model)` reads the model's planar-face topology (`geometry::feature`, the same B-rep `list_features` and the pick tools use).
  - A level, up-facing face is a **floor** when the facets across its outer ring rise from it and lean into it (a concave edge), and those walls face each other across the floor.
  - Walled all round, it is a **closed pocket**. With wall-less spans it is an **open pocket**. A straight channel (at least 2 widths long, both long sides walled, each end wholly walled or wholly open, area within 3% of the shape) is a **slot**, with each end open, round or square.
  - Each result carries:
    - the outer ring (world XY, counter-clockwise), island count and area;
    - floor Z, top Z (highest wall point) and depth;
    - the **tightest inside corner radius** (0 = sharp, `None` where no two walls meet) and the **open spans**;
    - for a slot: centreline ends, **width**, length and end kinds.
  - Shoulders, corner steps, top faces and a plate around a boss are not pockets.
- **`recognize::operation_for`** maps a feature onto `CreateOperation`'s inputs, so creating it is one undoable History step with every field editable:
  - a pocket (or a slot with a square closed end, which a round cap would leave standing) becomes a **2D Pocket** on a pick of the floor face, with `bottom_z` at the selection bottom and `top_z` at the selection bottom + depth;
  - a slot with round or open ends becomes a **Slot** along its centreline: width, fixed heights, source stock, open ends running full width out to the floor's edge.
- **MCP `detect_pockets {model, create?, tool?, name?}`** lists the features, each with the floor's `face:0x…` id (the id `list_features` prints) and the operation kind it would create. With `create` it adds that operation, one undo step.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/35-pocket-slot-recognition.md`.

Provenance: the concave-edge depression rule follows Joshi & Chang (CAD 20(2), 1988). The minimum-area rectangle follows Freeman & Shapira (CACM 18(7), 1975). No vendor material was consulted.

## How tested

Quick gate, debug: `pocket_recognition` 10/10, `mcp_pockets` 3/3, `mcp` 13/13, `mcp_pick` 7/7, `mcp_setup` 18/18, `cli` 2/2, `feature` 3/3. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Pinning tests, on watertight meshes built in code (`crates/app/tests/pocket_support`):
- `a_rectangular_pocket_is_closed_with_sharp_corners`
- `a_pocket_with_corner_radii_reports_its_tightest_corner` (r 4)
- `a_round_ended_closed_slot_is_a_slot_between_its_cap_centres`
- `a_through_slot_is_open_at_both_ends`
- `an_open_slot_with_a_square_end_machines_as_a_pocket`
- `parts_without_pockets_list_none` (plain block, shoulder, corner step, boss)
- `degenerate_input_refuses_cleanly` (unknown model; NaN, infinite and zero-area facets; a torn half mesh)
- `a_recognised_pocket_becomes_an_undoable_pocket_that_cuts_to_its_floor`: generates with no Gouge, reaches the floor, stays inside the ring; undo removes it
- `an_open_slot_machined_as_a_pocket_cuts_its_floor_without_a_gouge`
- `a_recognised_slot_becomes_a_slot_cut_along_its_centreline`: checks the path geometry exactly; undo removes it
- MCP: `detect_pockets_lists_a_rounded_pocket_and_creates_its_pocket` (generate + verify ok; undo/redo), `detect_pockets_creates_a_slot_for_a_through_slot`, `detect_pockets_refuses_bad_arguments_by_name`

## Not exercised / known gaps

- **#510 (filed):** every typed Slot whose cutter rides its round cap is reported as a gouge today, recognised or not. The likely cause is the stadium region's chorded caps measured against `GOUGE_TOL`. Until #510 lands, a recognised slot's Slot op refuses to post. Its test checks the path geometry, not the verifier's verdict.
- **Not recognised:**
  - through pockets / windows (no floor face);
  - non-level floors and tilted setup frames (the read is world +Z);
  - curved slots, T-slots and undercuts.
  - Each level of a stepped pocket is its own feature.
- An open pocket's open side is not written into the area controls' open boundary. The tool's corner radius stays uncut where a wall meets an open edge.
- **GUI entry point:** #511. Not exercised on real STEP parts or by hand. The release-tier heavy lanes were not run.

Changelog: Pocket and slot recognition - `detect_pockets` (MCP) lists a model's closed/open pockets and slots (depth, corner radius, slot width, open sides) and creates the Pocket or Slot that machines one, one undo step (#35)

Fixes #35

title: fix(app): a saved machine file keeps its key order
body:
**Stacked on #478** (#383, the Machines pane edits and saves `.mch` files). The #480 work is a95093c0.

## What changed
A `.mch` saved from the Machines pane keeps the key order it was read in. Keys the file didn't have go at the end of their object. Project files are untouched.

- **New `crates/app/src/machine/order.rs`** (with provenance).
  - It reads the source text once and records the key order of every object and array as a `KeyOrder` tree. A duplicated key keeps its first position and takes its last value, like `serde_json::Value`.
  - `to_pretty(value, order)` writes the same layout as `to_string_pretty` (2-space indent, `": "`), with keys in the recorded order, then any unknown keys sorted.
- **`MachineDraft`** gains `order: KeyOrder`. `open` and `from_template` fill it from the source, `blank` leaves it empty, and `text()` writes through `to_pretty`. Edits still act on the plain `serde_json::Value`, so `fields.rs` is unchanged.
- **No new dependency, and `serde_json/preserve_order` is not turned on workspace-wide.** That would change every JSON writer, project files included. `indexmap` is already in the lock file, but using it directly would still be a dependency change, and the order visitor is about 60 lines.
- The `docs/decisions/383-machines-edit.md` "key order" entry is replaced by this decision.

## How tested
- `machine_edit::a_saved_file_keeps_its_key_order_and_new_keys_go_last`: a hand-written file in deliberately unsorted order, with unknown keys, gets an edit plus a new `spindle`/`max_speed` block. The saved file's exact key list is checked.
- `machine_edit::a_new_machine_writes_the_same_text_serde_json_would`: with no recorded order, the output matches `to_string_pretty` byte for byte.
- `machine_edit`, `machine_library`, `machine` and `project_roundtrip` (69) pass. Project files are byte-identical; no project writer changed.
- `clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --tests -D warnings` is clean.

## Limitation
Only the key order is kept. A hand-written file's inline arrays (e.g. `[0, 0, 1]` on one line) still come out multi-line.

title: feat(app): fixture library - save, insert and delete user fixtures
body:
**Stacked on #482** (#339 slice 4, fixture UX), which is on #476. Slice 6 of #339 per the triage on the issue: a fixture library.

## What changed
**The library file.** One `fixtures.camfixtures` in the user fixtures folder: `CAMCRAFT_FIXTURES` (an absolute path), otherwise `<data dir>/camcraft/fixtures`, beside the machines folder.
- Versioned envelope: `{format: "camcraft-fixtures", version: 1, units: "mm", fixtures: [{name, note?, datum: {origin, rot}, facets}]}`. Save → load → save is byte-stable.
- **Refused by name, whole file:** bad JSON; wrong format, version or units; a missing name, datum or facets; a duplicate name; an empty mesh; a malformed facet; a rotation that isn't one; over 2M facets; the reserved `Machine/Table` name.
- A missing file reads as an empty library. A corrupt one is reported in the dialog, never shown as empty, and never overwritten.
- The atomic write mirrors #383's machine store. It's a short copy, to be folded into one helper once both land; see the decisions file.

**The datum.**
- An entry's facets are the fixture's own model-frame mesh, and its datum is a frame in that mesh.
- On insert, the model's pose is `P ∘ D⁻¹`, so the datum lands on the pick.
- The default datum is the model origin, so a fixture saved and re-inserted at its old pose stands exactly where it was. The other choice is "Bottom centre".

**Duplicate names:**
- In the library, saving an existing name asks "Replace …?". There is no silent rename.
- In the document, an inserted name that's taken lands as "Vise (2)", "Vise (3)" and so on.

**`InsertFixture`, one undo unit.** It spawns the model with the entry's facets, sets its pose, and tags it to the Fixtures node's setup. It refuses by name a setup that no longer exists, a non-finite or non-rotation pick, or a bad entry. There is no new project key: inserted fixtures are ordinary tagged models.

**Save and delete edit the library file.** They are save actions with confirmation, not undo entries, like machine files (#383).

**UI.** The setup's Fixtures node menu gains **Save fixture to library…** and **Insert from library…**, each a modal dialog.
- **Save:** the setup's fixtures as checkboxes, the datum choice, and a note.
- **Insert:** the entry list, X/Y/Z in display units, and roll/pitch/yaw. Buttons are Insert, **Delete from library…** (with confirmation) and Close.
- Picking the datum in the viewport is a follow-up.

All assets are user-made; no vendor libraries.

`docs/decisions/339-fixture-library.md`

## How tested
- App `fixture_library` (6 tests):
  - envelope round-trip, and refusals by name;
  - the folder resolver;
  - save, replace and delete file edits;
  - the datum placement maths;
  - insert with undo, redo and the project round-trip.
- UI `egui_app::fixture_library_tests` (4 tests, driven through the real dialog):
  - the menu rows;
  - save, then the replace confirmation;
  - Insert queues one undoable command, and delete happens only after confirmation;
  - a corrupt library is named in the dialog.
- Regressions green: app `fixture_ux` 8, `fixtures` 14, `commands_undo` 32, `fixture_mesh` 3; ui lib 352, ui `tests/fixtures` 7, `tests/models` 4. One #482 test's menu-label list now includes the two new rows.

- `clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --tests -D warnings` is clean.

A hands-on check. The test kit is prepared and sandboxed with `CAMCRAFT_FIXTURES`.

title: feat(mcp): serve the MCP tool table live from inside the GUI
body:
> Replaces #428, moved to the new fork (the old one left NeoTech's network; a push there closes the PR). Main is merged in; the one conflict was the module list in `mcp/mod.rs`, where both sides are kept. `mcp` 9/9, `mcp_live` 6/6 and `mcp_pick` 2/2 pass, and clippy for app and ui is clean. Still a draft, waiting on the hands-on GUI check (refreshed binaries `camcraft-ui-428` and `camcraft-cli-428`).

## What changed
The GUI can host the same MCP tool table (`app::mcp`) live, so an agent drives the open document and the user watches it in the viewport.

- **Opt-in, loopback only.** Off by default; started with `--mcp-port <n>` / `--mcp-port=<n>` or `CAMCRAFT_MCP_PORT` (flag wins; `0` picks a free port). Binds 127.0.0.1. A bad value exits 2.
- **Transport:** plain TCP carrying the same newline-delimited JSON-RPC as `camcraft-cli mcp`, plus a stdio<->TCP bridge `camcraft-cli mcp --connect <host:port>` so stdio MCP clients can attach.
- **Threading:** a std listener thread (one client at a time) only moves text; each line goes over an mpsc channel to the UI thread with its own reply channel and wakes the idle winit loop (`EventLoopProxy`). No world access off the UI thread.
- **Same document, same History.** The UI thread answers in `State::drain_actions` after the user's own queued commands, through the existing `Server` dispatch (no tool code duplicated): the `Env` gets the GUI's world handle and borrows the GUI's own `History` for the call. An agent step is one Ctrl+Z, and the agent's `undo`/`redo` walk the user's steps too. Every call bumps `doc_version`; the status line reads `agent: <tool>`.
- **Status strip** shows `MCP listening on 127.0.0.1:<port>` while the server runs (default frames unchanged).
- **Never crash:** malformed JSON -> -32700; a dropped client, closed channel or >16 MiB line is logged and the listener carries on; dropping the `Inbox` stops and joins the thread (~50 ms) at shutdown.
- **Refused live:** `open_project` (would replace the user's document past the unsaved-changes prompt).
- New code: `crates/app/src/mcp/{listen,live,bridge}.rs`, `crates/ui/src/mcp_host.rs`; `mcp/tools.rs` and `mcp/edit.rs` untouched.

## Maintainer note (judgement call)
There is no authentication: any local process can drive the open document while the server is on. Being off by default and loopback-only is the guard; a token could be added later if wanted. `save_project` without a path saves over the open project but does not mark it clean, so the app may still ask to save. A long `generate` blocks the UI frame for its duration.

## Readings
Debug, M5 Mac. `scripts/gate.sh quick` (camcraft-app + camcraft-ui suites): 1722 passed, 4 failed - all known reds on main (`setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…` #415; GPU headless trio). title: fix(app): the program sim sweeps a tap at its thread's minor diameter
body:
**Partial fix for #266.** This removes one of the two checks that refuse a tap on a normally modelled hole. The other one still blocks the post; see "What is left" below.

### What changed

- The program sim (the stock-sim clause of the post gate) swept a Tap-kind tool at its full major diameter. CAD models a tapped hole at the thread's minor (tap-drill) size, and a tap only cuts the thread band outside that wall. So the sim read the band as a gouge down the whole hole wall and refused the post.
- A Tap-kind tool now sweeps its thread's core: `diameter / 2 - 0.5413 x pitch`. That is the ISO 724 radial thread depth, the same constant the thread-mill generator already uses (`machining2d::THREAD_DEPTH_PER_PITCH`). For M6 x 1 the core is Ø4.917.
- The rule lives in one place, `operation::tool_law::cutting_radius`, so a later fix to the generator's verify can read the same number. Every other tool still sweeps half its diameter. A pitch too coarse to leave a core is refused by name.
- A tap over a hole smaller than its core, or over solid metal, is still a gouge.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/266-tap-minor-sweep.md`.

### Readings

| Case (M6 x 1 tap, plate with a blind hole) | Program sim before | Program sim after |
|---|---|---|
| Ø5 hole (tap drill) | gouge, worst 12.000 mm on the hole wall | clean, 0 gouge cells |
| Ø3 hole (too small) | gouge | gouge (still refused) |

### Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/tap_sim.rs`)

- `a_tap_in_a_hole_modelled_at_tap_drill_size_is_not_a_gouge`: fails on `main` (`worst 12.000 mm at (-0.31, -2.94, z 8.0)`), passes with the fix.
- `a_tap_wider_than_its_hole_is_still_a_gouge`: guards the other side; passes before and after.

### What ran (Windows 10, local)

- Both pinning tests alone, with the fix, and with `stock_sim.rs` put back to `main` (the first one fails there as above).
- `scripts/gate.ps1 -Tier quick`: app lib plus 13 suites (the gate map's `stock_sim` and `tool_law` suites plus `tap_sim`), 155 tests, all pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The app, through `camcraft-cli mcp`, built from this branch (upstream `main` 897a820 plus this commit): imported a plate STL with a round Ø5 blind hole, added `TAP-M6` and a Drill/Tap op, generated, verified. The program gate now reports `ok` with no problems. With a Ø3 hole it still reports `gouge: program cuts below the model in 127 cell(s), worst 6.00 mm`.
- Baseline batch tier on clean `main` 897a820 on this machine: all suites pass except three UI pixel snapshots (`egui_shell_snapshot`, `egui_shell_snapshot_light`, `tool_editor_snapshot`), which also fail without this change. Not run on Linux or macOS.

### What is left (why this is `Refs`, not `Fixes`)

With this fix the Ø5 tap job still does not post. The op's own verify flags `move 1 cuts past the finish surface` and `move 2 cuts past the finish surface` (the tap feeding in and out). That verify hands one tool radius (`tool.geom()`) to every law, including the rapids laws, where a tap's full diameter is the right envelope: a tap must never rapid into the thread band. I tried shrinking only the containment solid law's cutter; the tangency law still flags the same two moves, so I dropped that. Fixing it means splitting the cutting radius from the rapid envelope in the verifier's inputs, and it meets the convention in `solid_law_goldens.rs` that a tapped hole is modelled at the tap's major diameter. I left that for you to decide on the issue.

Changelog: The program sim no longer reads a tap's thread band as a gouge on a hole modelled at tap-drill size (#266, partial)
